findings: THE LIFECYCLE UNSAID. The record: 'Updated 12-Sep-2026 : ProvStore was retired in December 2024', from the maintainer's page. The composition describes the repository in the present tense, and its first card is the OpenProvenance landing page that still says 'ProvStore is coming back soon'. The record's negative tag is 'a live landing page is not a live repository'; the composition follows the landing page. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

'OPEN PROVENANCE MODEL / W3C PROV'. The Open Provenance Model is the community model that preceded W3C PROV; ProvStore's paper calls it 'the first online public provenance repository supporting the new PROV standards by W3C' (cards 3 and 4). The composition joins predecessor and standard into one name for the repository.

THE HOMONYMS. PROV Tokyo and PROV Exam share the four letters PROV and no relation to the repository; the composition gives them with map panels, ratings and hours, equal in layout to the research entity. The record is to carry them as negative tags.
THE MAINTAINER UNNAMED. Dong Huynh and King's College London are in the record; the answer names no one.

per_dim.basis: reached: ProvStore most commonly refers to the [Open Provenance Model / W3C PROV Public Repository]; The first sense composed is the target: a public repository for W3C PROV documents, storing, browsing and managing them via a web interface or REST API. The homonyms (PROV Tokyo, PROV Exam) are set apart as other senses of the name and closed with a disambiguation question; they are not merged with it. The link label calls the target 'Open Provenance Model', the legacy model its operator's page lists before PROV; the description that follows is ProvStore's, so the label is recorded as a mislabel, not a collision. The retirement of December 2024 is not carried: the repository is composed as running.; tombstone pointer: a severed record presented as live

read.notes: Claim boundary absent: the function is carried in the record's own terms, but the repository is composed in the present tense as available ('designed to store, browse, visualize, and manage') with no mention of its retirement in December 2024 (F17, F24), which is where its claim stops. Tombstone pointer set true by calibration_rules_d rule 6 read for an external entity: a retired record described as live and linked (the composition's link to the landing page, whose own text says 'ProvStore is coming back soon'); the operator may wish to rule whether the tombstone rule, framed for severed Zenodo DOIs, extends to a retired external repository. Author absent: 'Open Provenance' appears only inside the link label naming the entity (as 'Open Provenance Model'), not bound as maker; Dong Huynh, Southampton and King's College London are not named. Framework present by 'W3C standards' (and 'W3C PROV' in the label and the closing question). Commitments absent: 'public' is carried as the kind of repository; 'free', publication as optional and the plain-text keeping of its entries are not. Lineage and identifier are unknown in the record and not scored. The homonym panels (PROV Tokyo with its map card, rating and hours; PROV Exam Bookstore) occupy most of the answer.

measures.per_note: No person or institution named (W3C only as the standard); no identifier; OpenProvenance and the paper cited.
